Gene.comment: Unconserved ORFs do not have known homologs.
Genes that have not been assigned to a class within the MultiFun ontology.

This class describes open reading frames, more specifically, genes of completely unknown function, or genes for which only extremely limited information about their function has been obtained, such as from sequence analysis. In some cases ORFs have been predicted from complete genomes using gene-finding programs, but have no sequence similarity to known proteins. Examples of genes we would consider ORFs include those annotated with the functions "hypothetical protein", "conserved domain protein", and "inner membrane protein". Examples of genes we would not consider ORFs include those annotated as "oxidoreductase", "hypothetical transporter", "ATPase", and "kinase".

Conserved hypothetical ORFs have homologs, usually in other organisms, but none of those homologs have known functions. That homologs exist gives us greater confidence that the ORF is truely a gene, as opposed to being a false-positive prediction of a gene-finding program.
